subject.title: [Bug] Gateway swallows user-visible reply when an agent's exec stdout matches "configuration file" — replies=2 puts ⚠️ 🛠️ first, the actual reply second

question: Should this remaining work be treated as solved by Feishu answer-first coalescing, or should OpenClaw also change the exec/tool-warning policy so successful read-only or recovered exec output does not emit an extra visible warning?
rationale: Current main has a Feishu mitigation, but the still-current warning behavior is intentional in tests for mutating failures; deciding when to suppress false or recovered exec warnings affects user-visible diagnostics across channels.

options.title: Narrow False/Recovered Warning Fix
options.body: Preserve real mutating-tool warnings, but clear or suppress warnings when the trajectory proves the exec result was successful, read-only, or recovered before the final reply.

options.title: Accept Feishu Coalescing As Sufficient
options.body: Treat the current answer-before-warning behavior as good enough once live Feishu proof shows the real answer remains visible, leaving the extra warning as diagnostic output.

options.title: Broaden Exec Warning Suppression
options.body: Suppress exec warning finals after successful assistant replies more broadly, accepting the risk that valid diagnostics may become less visible.

recommendation.title: Narrow False/Recovered Warning Fix
recommendation.body: Preserve real mutating-tool warnings, but clear or suppress warnings when the trajectory proves the exec result was successful, read-only, or recovered before the final reply.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the current Feishu error-final preservation behavior and is the strongest routing owner for deciding whether that mitigation is sufficient for this Feishu-visible issue.
